transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-23
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 mins (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Rourke (Redwood SE), Harpreet Singh (CTO, NorthVertex), Dana Ortiz (Security Lead), Miguel Alvarez (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto):
Customer wants to validate Redwood for an internal search & summarization POC. Main asks: security/compliance gating (SOC2/ISO/SSO), RBAC and audit logging detail, and realistic benchmarks for latency and throughput. Discussed pilot acceptance criteria, dataset handling, and pilot timeline. Agreed to exchange security docs and run a short dedicated-node benchmark next week.

Topics:
- Pilot success criteria
- Workload sizing (qps, token profile)
- Benchmarks (p99 latency, throughput)
- Compliance: SOC 2 / ISO 27001, SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, KMS
- Deployment options (dedicated vs private VPC)

Action items (in call):
- Maya to send security summaries and SSO config notes
- Miguel to send traffic and endpoint samples
- Liam to schedule bench runs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, we'll try to keep this tight, the goal is to align on what's required for you to greenlight a short pilot.
[00:18] Harpreet: Yep thanks, we have a pretty strict gating checklist from security — SOC2, ISO, and SSO. We also want concrete latency/throughput numbers because search is a core path.
[00:28] Maya: Totally. Liam will lead the bench bits, I can cover onboarding and security docs. Quick intro, Liam —
[00:34] Liam: Hi all, Liam O'Rourke, I'm the SE working on inference performance. I do benchmarking and deployment configs.
[00:42] Dana: Hi, Dana — security lead. We're primarily concerned with auditability, key management and role-based access, plus how logs are retained and what data leaves our VPC.
[00:53] Maya: Great. Two quick clarifying Qs before we dive: what does a single user request look like today? avg tokens, any attachments? and what qps are you expecting for the pilot?
[01:08] Miguel: Most requests are short queries — 20 to 80 tokens on average, but we do have a tail where summarization jobs hit ~1k tokens. For pilot we'd aim for a 50 qps sustained, peaks of 150 qps for short bursts, but the important metric for us is p99 latency under load.
[01:26] Liam: OK that's helpful. So workload: mixture of short (20-80) and longer (500-1k). We'll recommend a quantized model for cost and a dedicated node for predictable latency in the pilot.
[01:40] Harpreet: When you say dedicated — we want to be clear on data isolation. Is that reserved capacity within Redwood-hosted or fully private VPC?
[01:49] Maya: Both are options. For pilot we typically recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) which gives logical isolation and no multi-tenant scheduling with encrypted disks; Private VPC is available if you require your own network controls or on-prem. For SOC2 gating both can be acceptable, but for strict residency or networking controls we'd look at Private.
[02:08] Dana: Can you explain the audit logs? We need immutable trails, user-level actions, token-level cost breakdown, and ability to export to our SIEM.
[02:20] Liam: Audit logs include API key usage, model/route changes, and per-request metadata — timestamps, run duration, approximate token counts (note: tokenization ambiguity in transcriptions — it's approximate). We can push logs to your S3 or syslog endpoint; retention is configurable, and we can provide log signing to detect tampering.
[02:41] Dana: So can logs be forwarded to our Splunk instance in near-real time?
[02:44] Maya: Yes, we support log forwarding, and for Private deployments you can keep logs inside your VPC; for hosted we forward securely.
[02:51] Harpreet: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys / HSM? Data-at-rest encryption?
[02:57] Liam: We support customer-managed KMS keys for Private and Dedicated; HSM-backed keys on the Private option. For hosted, we use provider KMS by default but can integrate with customer keys for enterprise contracts.
[03:10] Miguel: On RBAC — we need to limit model-pull and train/run operations for some teams. Do you expose fine-grained roles for model version pinning and deploy/rollback?
[03:19] Maya: Yes, RBAC is role-based and can be mapped to your IdP. You can separate deploy rights from call/consume rights. SSO is SAML/OIDC.
[03:27] Dana: We use SAML. One note, our IdP has nonstandard attribute mappings — can you handle that?
[03:33] Liam: We handle custom attribute mappings on SAML assertions; we usually request a metadata file and a sample assertion for mapping.
[03:39] Harpreet: Good. Back to success criteria — what do you recommend we measure during pilot to say yes/no?
[03:46] Maya: Typical pilot acceptance items: 1) functional parity for your top-3 flows (search, summarization short, summarization long), 2) p99 latency under sustained 50 qps below X ms — we should pick X together, 3) throughput headroom for bursts, 4) logs/audit exports working and verified, 5) SSO integration and RBAC applied for your users, 6) no P0 security gaps from your checklist.
[04:12] Miguel: For p99 we were thinking <200 ms for short queries, and <800 ms for long summarizations, is that realistic?
[04:20] Liam: For a quantized 13B-like variant on modern GPUs that seems plausible for short queries on a dedicated node. The long ones depend on decoding strategy and batch size; we can hit ~700 ms p99 with optimized kernel selection and prefix caching for 1k token outputs, but we'll need to test.
[04:37] Harpreet: Okay so we need a bench plan. What's the typical bench you run?
[04:42] Liam: We usually do three runs: a latency run (single-client steady low qps, measure p50/p95/p99), a throughput run (many concurrent clients to push qps until we see throughput plateau or latency SLOs break), and a mixed run that mimics your production tail patterns. Each run is 60 min for throughput, 15–20 min for latency.
[05:01] Miguel: Can you collect KV cache metrics? One of our apps uses long context and benefits from KV cache reuse.
[05:09] Liam: We expose cache hit rates and memory pressure metrics. In our telemetry we may label things slightly differently (key vee cache vs kv-cache sometimes), hope that won't throw your tooling.
[05:18] Dana: On compliance, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and ISO 27001 scope. Do you have an attestable report we can review quickly?
[05:27] Maya: We have an SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO 27001 cert for core platform — I'll send redacted versions. Also, we publish our control matrix that maps to common requirements. For pilot gating, security teams often accept the redacted SOC2 + control matrix and then request a narrow set of pen tests.
[05:45] Harpreet: Pen tests — do you allow an external vendor to run tests against a dedicated pilot instance?
[05:52] Liam: Yes, under a defined scope and schedule. For hosted we coordinate tests; for Private you can run from your network. We request a pre-approved plan and avoid tests that intentionally kill kernels or breach data.
[06:04] Harpreet: Data residency — some of our logs include EU resident PII. For pilot we need data not to leave eu-west-1, is that feasible?
[06:13] Maya: We can route workloads to a specific region and for Private deployments keep everything in your VPC. For hosted Dedicated we can also pin region for inference and logs.
[06:25] Miguel: One practical detail — our sample dataset contains semi-structured attachments. Can you redact attachments during ingestion or do we need to pre-process?
[06:33] Liam: We recommend client-side redaction pre-ingest for anything sensitive. We do have optional inline PII masking helpers in SDKs but they should not be relied on as sole gating for compliance.
[06:45] Dana: About observability and proofs — we need immutable audit trails for deploy changes and access. Are those signed and do you provide export hashes?
[06:54] Liam: We can enable append-only logs with HMAC signing; exportable daily manifests so you can verify integrity.
[07:02] Harpreet: Timeline — if we start next week, what does the pilot schedule look like?
[07:07] Maya: Typical pilot: week 0 onboarding + SSO + RBAC setup, week 1 run baseline bench and functional tests, week 2 iterate on config and run extended throughput runs, week 3 acceptance and wrap up. So roughly 3–4 weeks end-to-end.
[07:21] Miguel: That aligns. For week 0 we need integration documentation and a test account.
[07:26] Maya: We'll provision a sandbox and share runbooks.
[07:29] Dana: Can we try the SAML integration ahead of the bench? We want to ensure user mapping works before we run tests.
[07:34] Liam: Yes — that usually takes 1–2 days if we have your metadata.
[07:38] Harpreet: About model fallback — if the dedicated node is saturated do you have auto-fallback to a cheaper, higher-latency variant? We need graceful degradation.
[07:47] Liam: Yup, smart routing supports fallbacks by policy — you can specify a cost tier or a lower-latency target. For pilot we'll show how to configure that.
[07:55] Maya: Let's be explicit about acceptance criteria so legal and procurement have something concrete: 1) functional pass on top-3 flows; 2) p99 under agreed ceiling (we should pick numbers — Harpreet suggested 200 ms short / 800 ms long); 3) SSO integration with two power users and RBAC applied; 4) audit log exports validated to your SIEM; 5) SOC2/ISO docs reviewed and any open security items triaged as low-risk.
[08:24] Harpreet: Agreed but add 'no critical P0 security findings' as a gating item.
[08:28] Maya: Good point.
[08:30] Miguel: For bench instrumentation, can you give us exportable raw traces? We'll want them to feed our perf dashboards.
[08:36] Liam: Yes, we provide raw telemetry and a consolidated CSV of request latencies and token counts. For throughput runs we also include GPU utilization and kernel-level stats.
[08:46] Dana: Two smaller questions — rotation of API keys post-pilot, and retention windows for logs during the pilot.
[08:52] Maya: API key rotation is supported via the Console; we can automate rotation policies. Log retention defaults to 90 days on hosted but can be shortened; Private you control retention.
[09:02] Harpreet: OK, sounds good. Anything else on compliance?
[09:05] Dana: We'll run a short internal checklist once we have your SOC2 and ISO docs. Also need to know the chain of custody when we request logs for an audit.
[09:14] Liam: We can provide tamper-evident manifests and a signed chain-of-custody export on request.
[09:21] Harpreet: Let's talk about cost for the pilot — who covers dedicated node hours?
[09:25] Maya: For pilots we often provide a limited credit for the dedicated run; procurement can negotiate for longer pilots. We'll include a cost estimate in the follow-up.
[09:35] Miguel: One last technical note: we do fine-grained A/B on models, can Redwood support model pinning per-route for experiments?
[09:42] Liam: Yes, route-level model pinning and canary rollouts with automatic rollback if latency/regression thresholds are hit.
[09:49] Harpreet: OK, recap next steps?
[09:52] Maya: I'll send SOC2/ISO redacted reports, SSO metadata doc, RBAC sample. Liam will send bench plan and propose time slots for runs. Miguel will send traffic profile. We tentatively target bench week of 9/27.
[10:07] Dana: Sounds good. A couple typos from my notes: please clarify log forwarding latency and sample format.
[10:14] Maya: We'll include sample payloads and retention agreements in the email.
[10:18] Harpreet: Cool. Thanks everyone.
[10:20] (call end)

Notes on transcript quality: auto-transcription sometimes mislabels acronyms (SAML as 'sam-el'), and some proper nouns may be off. There was brief crosstalk around 04:30.

Appendix — Proposed pilot acceptance checklist (text copy):
- Functional pass: top-3 flows validated with sample data
- Performance: p99(short) < 200ms, p99(long) < 800ms (adjustable after initial runs)
- Security: SSO via SAML configured, RBAC applied, SOC2/ISO docs reviewed, no P0 findings
- Observability: audit logs forwarded to customer SIEM, integrity manifests provided
- Data controls: KMS integration confirmed, region pinned to eu-west-1 (if required)

References mentioned:
- Redwood security control matrix (link to be sent)
- Bench runbook (Liam to share)
- Sample SAML metadata (customer to provide)
